nodes.name: DLP 3D printing of Ni electrodes
nodes.procedure: Gyroid structure with Janus porosity was fabricated by DLP technology using Ni-based precursors to produce 3DP Ni-S (small pore size), 3DP Ni-L (large pore size), and 3DP Ni-G (gradient pore size, Janus porosity).
nodes.source_text: the gyroid structure with Janus porosity was fabricated by DLP technology due to the desirable surface area and efficient bubble behaviors.

nodes.name: In situ growth of Ru-Ni(OH)₂
nodes.procedure: The Ni-based gradient electrodes with Janus porosity were simply submerged in RuCl₃ solutions at room temperature. Chlorine ions will adsorb on the passivation film of the metal electrode, thus destroying the film and accelerating the corrosion of the Ni electrode. Moreover, hydroxide ions, which are generated through the reaction between water and dissolved oxygen in the solution, will migrate toward the surface of the 3DP Ni electrode. Owing to the inclusion of Ru³⁺ ions into the chloride ion-containing solution, layered hydroxides containing Ru will spontaneously precipitate onto the surface of the metal electrode, respectively. The proportion of Ni and Ru content was presented in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show uniform distribution of metallic Ru nanoparticles on the Ni(OH)2 surface for Ru-Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) images illustrate the uniform distribution of metallic Ru nanoparticles on the Ni(OH)2 surface (Figure S12, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV fitting plots show Cdl of 94.5 mF cm^{-2} for Ru-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-G, verifying large ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) value of Ru-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-G is 94.5 mF cm^{-2}... which verifies the Ru-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-G can maintain a large enough ECSA to promote the reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV fitting plots show Cdl of 101.3 mF cm^{-2} for Fe-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-G.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Fe-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-G exhibits the Cdl value of 101.3 mF cm^{-2}, where the value is intermediate between Fe-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-S (103.7 mF cm^{-2}) and Fe-Ni(OH)2/3DP Ni-L (100.8 mF cm^{-2}), describing the initial factor of the excellent OER performance.
